title: Extrema of Piecewise and Absolute-Value Functions
quickIdea: When a formula changes at a point, or contains an absolute value, the join itself is a candidate - and it is often where the extremum lives.
remember: For f = max{g, h} or f = min{g, h}, the formula changes exactly where g(x) = h(x); solve that equation to get the candidate points.
At a join, compare the one-sided derivatives: unequal slopes mean a corner, and a corner can be an extremum.
For a function of the form -(something)^2, the maximum is where the squared term vanishes and the value is 0.
Write the absolute value as two linear pieces before differentiating; |x| = x for x >= 0 and -x for x < 0.

A function can be continuous everywhere, have a local maximum, have a continuous derivative, and still have a derivative that is not differentiable everywhere - GATE CSE 2026 Set 1 Q.36 is exactly this chain.

example.prompt: GATE CSE 2026 Set 1 Q.36: for f(x) = (|x|/2 - x)(x - |x|/2), decide whether f has a local maximum, whether f has a local minimum, whether f' is continuous on R, and whether f' is not differentiable on R.
example.work: The second factor is the negative of the first, so f(x) = -(|x|/2 - x)^2, which is <= 0 with equality only at x = 0. Hence f(0) = 0 is a strict global (and local) maximum and there is no local minimum. For x >= 0, |x|/2 - x = -x/2 so f = -x^2/4 and f' = -x/2. For x < 0, |x|/2 - x = -3x/2 so f = -9x^2/4 and f' = -9x/2. At 0 the difference quotient is -h/4 for h > 0 and -9h/4 for h < 0, both tending to 0, so f'(0) = 0 and f' is continuous at 0, hence on R. But the one-sided derivatives of f' at 0 are -1/2 and -9/2, which differ, so f' is not differentiable at 0.
example.answer: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are true and statement 2 is false: f has a local maximum, f' is continuous on R, and f' is not differentiable over R. The accepted answer on GATE Overflow is A, C, D.

gateAngle: GATE CSE 2026 Set 1 Q.36 and 2024 Set 1 Q.1 both build a function out of a max or an absolute value and ask where it is differentiable or extremal. The exam's method is always the same: split at the joins, write one formula per piece, then read the derivative on each side.

variations.label: VERIFIED PYQ
variations.question: GATE CSE 2026 Set 1 Q.36: which statements about f(x) = (|x|/2 - x)(x - |x|/2) are true?
variations.answer: f has a local maximum; f' is continuous over R; f' is not differentiable over R.
variations.why: f = -(|x|/2 - x)^2 peaks at 0, its derivative is the continuous but kinked function -x/2 for x > 0 and -9x/2 for x < 0.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: Let g(x) = min{x^2, x}. Where does g have local extrema?
variations.answer: None. g(x) = x for x <= 0, x^2 for 0 < x < 1 and x for x >= 1, and g is strictly increasing on the whole line: at 0 the left piece rises to 0 and the right piece rises away from 0, and at 1 both pieces approach 1 from below and leave it upwards.
variations.why: It is the counterweight to max{x, x^3}: a join is a candidate, not an extremum, and here neither join qualifies. Assuming every change of formula is a corner-and-extremum gives two wrong answers.

trap.what: Differentiating a piecewise or absolute-value function without first splitting it, so the join is never tested.
trap.why: The join is where the formula changes; the derivative there is one-sided and may not exist, and it is frequently the only extremum.
trap.counterexample: f(x) = |x| has its only minimum at the join 0, where no two-sided derivative exists. In the 2026 question the maximum is at the join 0, where the two pieces have slopes -0.5 and -4.5 approaching it.

check.question: For f(x) = (|x|/2 - x)(x - |x|/2), what is f(1) and f(-1)?
check.explanation: At 1 the pieces give -x^2/4 = -1/4; at -1 they give -9x^2/4 = -9/4. Both are below f(0) = 0, which confirms the maximum at 0.
